Sensor noise on y is small (<~0.01) so trends and end-slope in measured_summary are interpretable.

submission.machine_card: Electric heater, positive gain: more power = hotter. Self-draining: u=0 falls from 0.544 to 0.319 in 180s still falling -0.0011/s, ambient <=0.2 likely ~0.04-0.15. No dead-zone: u=0.3-0.5 all move. Lag: flat 15-40s after steps (E1 15s, E2 ~25s, E3 ~40s) + dominant tau ~150-250s (180s holds not fully settled except after 360s at 0.3). Gain: incremental 1.42 between 0.3/0.34 equilibria, average ~0.7-0.9 from 0.2 baseline. Steady points: (u=0.3,y=0.469 slope 0), (u=0.34,y=0.526 slope 0.0001), (u=0.5,y~0.50-0.52 still rising 0.0007 after 180s). Hold for target 0.5 needs u~0.322 interpolated. Noise on y ~0.005-0.01. Speed: worst-case 0.006/s per u, observed avg ~0.001-0.002/s.
submission.design_rationale: First-order self-draining heater with long lag. Feedforward 0.322 centers output at target 0.5 from bracketing equilibria (u=0.3->0.469 settled slope 0, u=0.34->0.526 slope 0.0001) with incremental gain 1.425 (0.057/0.04). PI corrects residual: Kp=0.7 gives loop gain ~1.0 with K~1.2-1.4, stable against 15-40s dead-time and tau 150-250s. Ki=0.01 (Ti=70s) trims FF error within settling window; gated to 20% when |e|>0.15 to avoid windup during cold heat-up. D on filtered measurement Kd=8 with 20s filter damps lag overshoot, clamped to +/-0.12 for noise. Filter tau 12s smooths 0.005-0.01 noise. Integral clamp +/-0.25 leaves 0.25 authority, >3x max expected FF error 0.02-0.05, so no permanent offset. Output capped 0.75 plus yf>0.7/0.8 cutback keeps y far from 0.85 soft / 0.9 hard cutoff.
submission.predicted_behavior: From cold 0.2: initial u~0.53-0.59, rise with ~150-200s to band, enter band ~150-220s, settle within +/-0.025 by <300s. Small overshoot <0.015 above 0.5 due to lag, then converge. Steady u ~0.30-0.34 centered 0.322, MAE after 300s <0.012, in-band >90%, energy ~0.10 per s (u^2~0.10). From near band: settle <120s with no overshoot beyond 0.55. Never exceeds 0.70 in normal tracking.
self_test_expectations: control returns finite float in [0,1] for noisy y, varying dt, first call with {}
steady hold: with y=0.5 target 0.5 and settled filter, u stays 0.25-0.40
cold start e=0.3 gives u 0.45-0.65, not saturated to 0 or 1
safety: with yf>0.8 output is 0.0-0.15, never drives toward 0.9 cutoff

no exception, no override, no import beyond math

submission.diagnosis: Response is slower (larger lag/delay), not weaker gain or larger loss or sensor shift. Grounding: discovery E4 u=0.3 settles 0.469 slope 0.0 and E6 u=0.34 settles 0.526 slope ~0.0001 bracket u_ss~0.32 for 0.5; evaluation closed-loop holds y_mean 0.489-0.492 with u_mean 0.292-0.295, i.e. within ~0.02 of nominal once integrator offset (+0.01 error, integral ~-0.04 after long overshoot) is accounted for, not the +0.10-0.15 shift expected if K halved or loss doubled. Zero-input decay test was not rerun after change, but closed-loop decay after peak (0.604 at ~312s to 0.59 at 360s to 0.53 at ~510s with u~0.29-0.33) is much slower than E2 cooling (0.544 to 0.319 in 179s at u=0), consistent with same loss but delayed response. Failure mode is classic delay overshoot: from cold 0.04-0.05 with u~0.64-0.66, y stays flat ~30s then rises to 0.59-0.61 at 300-324s (+0.09 above band) and stays high until ~500s then sags to 0.46-0.49 until 900s, giving in-band 0.575-0.640 vs 0.70 required. Estimated new dead-time ~45-60s vs old 15-40s (+~25s) and tau ~200-250s vs old 130-180s (+50-70s, ~40% slower); steady gain unchanged within ~5%.
submission.change_summary: Lowered proportional kick (Kp 0.7->0.5 with +-0.25 clamp) and derivative (Kd 8->4, clip +-0.10, Td 20->15, Tf 12->10) to add phase margin for larger lag; strengthened integral (Ki 0.01->0.028, limits +-0.20, reduced when |e|>0.12) with conditional anti-windup to recover from post-overshoot droop without windup; kept nominal feedforward 0.322+0.70*(target-0.5) but made it adaptive by slowly transferring settled integral into ff (lam=0.005*dt when |e|<0.05) and tracking target changes; raised Umax 0.75->0.80 with P-clamp so effective cold-start drive is ~0.55 not 0.65 (less stored heat) but high power remains available if gain falls; kept 0.70/0.80 safety caps.
submission.machine_card: Adaptive FF + filtered PID-D on measurement for first-order heater (tau ~150-250s, dead-time ~20-60s, K~1.4 y/u). Nominal ff 0.322 for target 0.5, auto-trims to 0.05-0.75. Kp 0.5, Ki 0.028, Kd 4.0. Operates y in [0,1], target ~0.5, dt 0.2-5s, noisy y. Output 0-0.80 (hard 0-1), safety cut to 0.20 above 0.70 and 0 above 0.80. For cold starts, limits initial drive to ~0.55-0.60 to prevent overshoot while still entering band by ~130s nominal / ~210s slowed.
submission.design_rationale: Slower lag leaves steady-state unchanged so fixed ff 0.322 remains correct on average but transient needs less aggressive P and better-damped D. Smaller Kp + P-clamp reduces heat stored during 100-150s rise that later appears as 0.09 overshoot. Smaller Kd with shorter Td still brakes rise but does not amplify delay-induced phase lag. Larger Ki removes the long 0.47-0.49 tail that caused most out-of-band time after 500s, while conditional integration and saturation freeze prevent windup during the initial 0.45 error. Adaptive ff learns u_ss online (u~0.29-0.32 for 0.5) so both nominal (u_ss~0.32) and changed plant are held without permanent integral offset, and target-shift logic preserves nominal behavior if target moves. Safety caps guarantee no soft-limit violation.
submission.predicted_behavior: If lag hypothesis is correct, cold start from ~0.05 will enter 0.475-0.525 by ~130-160s nominal and ~180-220s slowed, peak <0.55-0.56 (vs 0.60-0.61 before), settle inside band by ~250-280s and stay there, giving in-band after 300s >0.80 (vs 0.63), MAE <0.025 (vs 0.036), u_ss ~0.30-0.33, energy similar ~110-125, zero overrides/hard violations. Nominal plant will also pass because ff remains ~0.32 and lower Kp still meets rise-time with less overshoot.

submission.diagnosis: Nominal from E1-E6: ambient ~0.20, gain ~0.93 (0.3->0.469, 0.34->0.526), tau 130-180s, dead-time 15-40s, u_ss(0.5)~0.32. Post-change hidden v2 episodes: early heating 0.05->0.18 in 60s at u~0.62 vs nominal 0.178 expected, later 0.013 rise in 60s for du=0.14 vs 0.04 expected (~3x small); cut of du~0.5 for 80s (t260-340) drops y only 0.046 vs 0.186 expected nominal (~4x small); low-u decay at y~0.57 with u~0.10 is 0.0009/s vs E2 zero-input 0.0012/s at y~0.53 (within 25%, so loss unchanged). Yet overshoot to 0.61-0.63 persists and v2 enters sustained ~250s period oscillation (0.40-0.63) while v1 on same cold start was smooth. Weaker gain alone would lower loop gain and be more stable, outflow increase would speed decay - neither seen. Pattern is classic longer lag/delay: sluggish response + preserved zero-input decay + increased overshoot/oscillation. Estimate new dead-time 65-80s (+40-50s) and tau 260-300s (~1.8-1.9x). Designed for delay 75s, tau 280s.
submission.change_summary: Kept feedforward+PI structure but retuned for ~+45s delay and ~1.8x tau: lowered Kp to 0.55 and Ki to 0.014 with tight anti-windup (+/-0.15), replaced raw D with lead-compensated P on predicted y (Tp=35s, y_pred=yf+Tp*df, p=Kp*(target-y_pred)) to brake early despite delay, kept Tf=8s/Td=12s filtering and 0.80/0.70/0.80 safety caps, and made feedforward slowly adapt to u when |e|<0.04 and |df|<0.001 with bumpless transfer. This damps delay-induced overshoot/limit-cycle while still heating aggressively when far and re-learning u_ss if gain drifts.
submission.machine_card: Heater y in [0,1], u in [0,1]. Nominal: y_ss=ambient+K*u, ambient~0.20 (hidden cold-start ~0.05), K~0.93, tau~150s, dead-time~25s, u_ss(0.5)~0.32. Changed: K and ambient/loss similar (decay 0.0009 vs 0.0012/s), dead-time~70s, tau~280s. Requires lead compensation and lower PI gains; ff 0.05-0.75, Umax 0.80, soft cap 0.20 above 0.70, cutoff at 0.80/0.90.
submission.design_rationale: Delay increase cannot be fixed by higher integral - it causes hunting. Fix is phase lead: control predicted y 35s ahead, lower loop gain, filter derivative, freeze/slow integral when far or saturated, and adapt ff only when settled. Tp=35s compensates ~70s new dead-time without over-leading nominal 25s plant (still stable, slightly overdamped). Ki 0.014 gives ~2x phase margin vs old 0.028. I limits prevent windup during 200s warmup. ff adaptation recovers correct bias 0.32 nominal or new value without fighting integral.
